audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers label the lane EVEN at 5.5/10 and give Sejuani or Skill five of seven stages, while the prose says Shen wins levels 1-5 outright and the Emerald+ win rate is 45.07% over 142 games.
audit.why: The level chart contradicts the whys that sit directly beneath it. Shen's Twilight Assault empowers two autos before Sejuani has a Frost stack, and Shadow Dash is up from level 2.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Shen / Shen / Shen / Shen / Shen / Skill / Skill in both layers, matching the packet stage read and the existing prose. Difficulty stays 5.5/10 EVEN because the matchup genuinely equalises once Sunfire lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text carried no cooldown numbers, so 'track his taunt' had nothing to count.
audit.why: Shadow Dash is 18/16/14/12/10s and Stand United is 200/180/160s. Those two numbers are the whole rhythm of this lane.
audit.corrected: Shadow Dash written as 18s at rank 1 and 14s at rank 3; Stand United written as 200s at rank 1 in the level-6 phase and in mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five fields claim Spirit's Refuge blocks Sejuani's Frost build-up entirely, calling the trade template unusable.
audit.why: Riot's text for Spirit's Refuge is 'Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked' — attacks, not spells. Winter's Wrath is the ability that applies Frost stacks per Sejuani's own kit text, so both mace arcs land inside the zone and Permafrost still arms. The old advice to wait out the refuge before swinging W throws away the trade.
audit.corrected: Spirit's Refuge blocks attacks, not spells. Swing both Winter's Wrath arcs inside the zone during the taunt and fire Permafrost the instant Frost caps.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns tells the player to count Shadow Dash without a number.
audit.why: Flagged only — the cooldowns string is shared boilerplate and the number now lives in the phases and spikes text where the player reads it.
audit.corrected: Left in place; numbers added where they are actionable.

edits.after: Shen wins level 1 outright — Twilight Assault (Q) recalls his spirit blade to empower two autos with max-health damage before you have a single Frost stack. Walk up to last-hit only. At level 2 he can Shadow Dash (E) to taunt you and pop Spirit's Refuge (W), and here is the detail that decides the lane: Spirit's Refuge blocks attacks, not spells. Winter's Wrath is the ability that applies Frost stacks, so both mace arcs land inside his zone and Permafrost still arms. What you must not do is stand in the taunt auto-attacking into the block. At level 3 he still initiates first — eat the taunt, swing W twice while the refuge blocks nothing, then E-stun him as he walks out. Take Doran's Shield and Second Wind and play for the gank that decides the lane.
edits.before: Shen wins the level-1 scrub instantly — his Q (Twilight Assault) empowers two autos with on-hit damage before you have a single Frost stack. Walk up to last-hit only, never auto-trade on the wave. At level 2 he can Shadow Dash (E) to taunt you and immediately pop Spirit's Refuge (W), blocking every auto you land for the full taunt duration; your Frost-stack combo needs autos to function and he just negates them entirely. At level 3 your Q+W+E chain can theoretically stun him, but he gets to initiate with E into W first — you take the taunt damage and his auto block THEN try to stun him as he walks away healthy. Take Doran's Shield and Second Wind, accept that these three levels belong to him, and save your HP for the gank that will decide the lane.

edits.after: Levels 4-5 he walks up, empowers autos with Q, taunts with Shadow Dash — 14 seconds at rank 3 — and leaves with more HP than he started. Answer it correctly: the moment the taunt lands, swing both Winter's Wrath arcs, because Spirit's Refuge only stops attacks and your mace still stacks Frost. Fire Permafrost the instant Frost caps rather than waiting for the refuge to expire; waiting is how this trade gets lost. At level 6 you get Glacial Prison and he gets Stand United on a 200-second cooldown — if you back off to farm he channels it and wins a fight elsewhere, and if you shove he taunt-trades you again. Shove fast, back, and track that 200 seconds so you know when the lane door is open.
edits.before: Levels 4–5 are more of the same: his Q resets quickly and he will walk up, hit Q, E-taunt into W, then walk out with more HP than he started. Do not answer the taunt engage by trying to W-E immediately — wait for Spirit's Refuge to drop, then hit W (both swings) to stack Frost and fire E only when he is outside the auto-block zone. At level 6 you get Glacial Prison but so does he get Stand United — if you back off to farm, he channels global R and wins a fight elsewhere; if you shove, he taunt-trades you again. Your R is better in a straight 5v5 but his is better spread across the map. Play level 6 by shoving fast, backing, and tracking his R cooldown on the minimap so you know exactly when the lane door is open.

notes: The buried headline: Spirit's Refuge blocks attacks, not spells, and Winter's Wrath is a spell. Five fields told the player his W negates Sejuani's Frost combo and to wait it out — that instruction loses the trade every time. Also note the level chart on disk gave Sejuani or Skill five stages in a 45.07% matchup whose own whys say Shen wins levels 1-5; I aligned it to the prose. I did not assert anything about Sejuani's basic attacks applying Frost: Riot's kit text credits Frost stacks only to Winter's Wrath, so all corrected text routes the stacks through W.
